title: How a nephron turns blood into urine

stages.label: Glomerulus filters
stages.note: Pressure pushes fluid out of the blood

stages.label: Good stuff back

explain.say: Each kidney contains about a million tiny filtering units called nephrons. Each nephron is a long, looped tube that turns some of your blood plasma into urine.

stages.label: Good stuff back
stages.ask: Why does the kidney take things back after filtering?

explain.say: It starts at the glomerulus, a knot of tiny blood vessels. Blood pressure pushes water, salts, sugar and wastes out through its walls into a cup around it, but keeps blood cells and big proteins in.

stages.label: Glomerulus filters
stages.note: Pressure pushes fluid out of the blood

stages.label: Good stuff back
stages.ask: Why does the kidney take things back after filtering?

explain.say: That filtered fluid flows along the tubule. Its walls pull almost everything useful back into the blood: all the sugar, most of the salts and about 99 percent of the water.

stages.label: Glomerulus filters
stages.note: Pressure pushes fluid out of the blood

stages.label: Good stuff back
stages.ask: Why does the kidney take things back after filtering?

explain.say: What is left, mostly water, urea and extra salts, passes through the loop of Henle and collecting duct, where the final amount of water is adjusted. Then it drains down to the bladder as urine.

faq.a: A nephron is one of the tiny filtering units of the kidney. Each kidney has about a million. A nephron filters blood at the glomerulus and then adjusts the fluid in its tubule to make urine.
asks: How many nephrons are in a kidney?

faq.a: The glomerulus is a ball of very thin, leaky capillaries. Blood pressure squeezes water and small molecules out of the blood into the nephron, while cells and large proteins stay in the blood.
asks: Tell me about the glomerulus filtering

faq.q: Why does the kidney take things back after filtering?
faq.a: The filter is not choosy: it lets out useful things like sugar, salts and water along with wastes. The tubule then pulls back what the body needs, so only wastes and spare water leave as urine.
asks: Tell me about the good stuff going back

faq.a: Urine is mostly water with urea, a waste made from breaking down proteins, plus salts and small amounts of other wastes.

faq.q: How much fluid do kidneys filter each day?
faq.a: Together the kidneys filter about 180 litres of fluid a day, but they put almost all of it back, so only about 1 to 2 litres leaves as urine.
asks: How much blood do kidneys clean?

facts: Each human kidney contains roughly one million nephrons.
The kidneys filter about 180 litres of fluid a day and return about 99 percent of it to the blood.
